description: Pixel dimensions plus print DPI gives the real-world print size in inches and cm — with a quality warning when DPI drops below 150.

faqs.a: 300 DPI is the standard for sharp photographic prints. 150 DPI is the practical minimum for close viewing; below that, prints look soft or pixelated.
faqs.q: What DPI should I use for printing photos?

faqs.a: Print size = pixels ÷ DPI. A 6000 × 4000 px image at 300 DPI prints at 20 × 13.3 inches.
faqs.q: How do I calculate print size from pixels?

faqs.a: Very large prints (posters, banners) are viewed from far away, so 100–150 DPI can still look fine. This tool flags quality relative to close-up viewing.
faqs.q: Why is 150 DPI acceptable for posters but not small prints?

howto: Enter the image's pixel width and height.
Read the print size in inches and centimetres plus the quality rating.
